name: Grid wave propagation

source.description: Four inspected references animate fields of tiles, shapes, dots or pixels in waves spreading from a point.

technique: Every cell of a grid changes state with a delay proportional to its distance from an origin, so a pattern change becomes a visible ripple and a transition gains a source and direction.
purpose: Make pattern, data or texture feel alive; turn a scene change into a wave; express propagation (signals, spreading, adoption).
visual_behaviour: Tiles pop, flip or change colour starting at the centre (or a corner) and spreading outward over 0.5-1.5 s.
mechanics: Grid stagger with an 'amount' for the whole wave; per-cell tween 0.3-0.5 s; flips rotate quarter turns so Truchet arcs reconnect.

decomposition.timing: Observed waves cross the frame in about 1-2 s (ref-92c22222a2 7.58-9.58 s).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Origin: center, start, end, edges, index or [x, y]

failure_modes: Too many cells (DOM cost, moire at 720p)
Uniform waves with no origin read as a fade
Pattern detail below the frame-review blank-frame threshold

implementation.approach: Studio.draw.grid builds cells (optional Truchet tiles); Studio.fx.gridWave staggers a preset over the grid; consecutive flips chain.

measurements.what: every-frame preview capture of tests/reference-derived/shape-and-grid (144 Truchet cells, three waves)
measurements.value: 51.9 ms/frame median, 94.9 ms max, peak headless Chromium 307 MB, 469 DOM nodes

limitations: DOM cells; thousands of cells would need a canvas renderer with a seek-safe draw hook

provenance.observed: A square subdivides into Truchet-like tiles; a colour change propagates outward from the centre.
Geometric tiles (circles, quarter circles, squares) pop into a grid in a staggered sweep.
A dot grid rises into a field of cubes in a wave (rendered in 3D in the reference).
A pixel-block grid fills behind a word card.

evidence.notes: Pop wave from the centre and two flip waves inspected.

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown). Truchet tiling is a centuries-old public pattern family.
